clue.text: Mended pliers and another tool to make fake backing

indicators.note: something mended has been put back together, so the letters of pliers are reassembled

parts.note: a vice is a workshop tool for gripping, a second tool after the pliers

explanation.surface: A handyman repairs pliers and uses a second tool to make a backing that only looks genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: Lip service is support professed in words but not meant, which is backing that is fake.

clue.text: Wealth loses its core attraction

indicators.note: the middle letter of the five-letter word for wealth is dropped

parts.note: lucre is money or wealth, usually ill-gotten

explanation.surface: A rich person's money stops being appealing once its heart is gone.
explanation.definitionFit: A lure is something that tempts or draws in, a synonym for an attraction.

clue.text: Ward for example toured by publicity person, note

parts.note: a PRO is a public relations officer

indicators.note: the two letters for example are travelled around, so enclosed, by the following pieces

parts.note: TE is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
EG is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: A publicist shows a hospital ward round, for instance, and makes a note of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A ward is someone under the protection of a guardian, close to a protege, a person guided by a patron.

clue.text: Cab boss, English, in east supported by club

indicators.note: in a down clue the last piece sits beneath the others, holding them up

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east
a driver is a golf club used off the tee

explanation.surface: A taxi firm's English boss, based in the east, has a club behind him.
explanation.walkthrough: The cab here is the driver's compartment of a locomotive, not a taxi.
explanation.definitionFit: The person in charge of a locomotive's cab is the one who drives the train.

clue.text: It spins five or nearly ten times

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

indicators.note: nearly means the word ten is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: ten spelt out
X is the multiplication sign

explanation.surface: Something spinning, at five or almost ten times the rate.
explanation.definitionFit: A vortex is a whirling mass of water or air, something that spins round.

clue.text: Our beginning or our end, Mass excepted?

indicators.note: excepted means left out, so the letter for mass is removed

parts.note: cremation is one way our bodies end up after death
M is the physics symbol for mass

explanation.surface: A theological musing: was Creation our start, or our finish, leaving out the Mass?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' looks like the church service; it is only the letter M.
explanation.definitionFit: The Creation, in the biblical account, is where humanity began.

clue.text: Press article hidden among manuscripts

indicators.note: the article is tucked inside the abbreviation for manuscripts

parts.note: A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper article lies buried in a pile of manuscripts.
explanation.definitionFit: A press of people is a crowd, a dense throng or mass.

clue.text: Embarrassed when this writer has fooled around

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'

indicators.note: the word for fooled goes round the setter's pronoun

parts.note: to have been had is slang for having been fooled
the setter refers to themselves as me

explanation.surface: Someone is mortified because the writer has been messing about.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashamed means feeling embarrassment or guilt over one's conduct.

clue.text: Not the best assistant to judge

parts.note: a second is a helper, as to a boxer or duellist
to rate is to judge or assess

explanation.surface: An assistant is not the best person to act as judge.
explanation.definitionFit: Second-rate means of inferior quality, falling short of the top grade.

clue.text: Run out of good English wood for site with raised beds?

parts.note: RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out
the Forest of Arden is an ancient woodland in Warwickshire, England

explanation.surface: Someone runs out of good English timber.
explanation.walkthrough: The Forest of Arden is the setting of Shakespeare's As You Like It.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants on a rooftop grow in beds raised high above the street, a playful take on raised beds.

clue.text: Elegant edible plant stops short of old railway

indicators.note: the plant's name halts before reaching the letters for old railway, so they are cut off its end

parts.note: chicory is a salad plant whose root is also used as a coffee substitute

explanation.surface: A smart vegetable patch ends just before a disused railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic means stylish and fashionable, a synonym for elegant.

clue.text: Fixing cold-water pump almost makes toilet drier

indicators.note: fixing a broken pump means putting its parts back in order, so these letters are rearranged
almost means the word pump loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Repairing a cold-water pump nearly turns a lavatory into a dry one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toilet' here means washing and dressing, as in toilet water, not a lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Talc is dusted on the skin after a bath, drying it as part of one's toilet, the grooming routine.

clue.text: Distant cousin cultivating the land near isle

indicators.note: cultivating land turns it over, so these letters are dug over into a new order

parts.note: the Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A farming relative works the fields near an island.
explanation.definitionFit: This early human species is a close but extinct relative of modern humans, a cousin far back in time.

clue.text: Family member in stage role swallowing nut

parts.note: a step is a stage in a process

indicators.note: the word for role takes the printer's unit inside it

parts.note: a part is a role in a play
an en, also called a nut, is a printer's measure of spacing

explanation.surface: A relative playing a part on stage eats a nut.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent by marriage to one's mother or father belongs to the family without being a blood relation.

clue.text: 10 hear about goal

definitions.note: refers to the answer to 10 across, meaning elegant

indicators.note: the word for hear goes round the word for goal

parts.note: to try a case is to hear it in court
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A court hears a case about scoring a goal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are synonyms meaning stylish and in the latest fashion.

clue.text: He gives up clubs formerly associated with the German

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
once means formerly
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: Someone resigns from clubs he once shared with a German.
explanation.definitionFit: One who concedes yields or admits defeat, a person who gives up.

clue.text: Novel treat devoured by 52 bookworms?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are swallowed up inside the Roman numeral

parts.note: LII is 52 in Roman numerals, L for fifty and II for two

indicators.note: novel means new and unusual, so the letters of treat are given a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A new novel is a treat gobbled up by keen readers.
explanation.walkthrough: The online clue lost the word 'treat'; the printed paper had it. 'Novel' looks like the book being devoured, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The literati are well-read, learned people, which avid readers jokingly called bookworms may be.

clue.text: Fertile academic ringing large one in charge

indicators.note: the academic encircles the letters for large and one

parts.note: PROF is short for professor
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A productive professor phones a big boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Prolific means producing abundantly, as a fertile plant or writer does.

clue.text: Work problem involves very big animal

indicators.note: the work and problem together take the outsize letters inside

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
a sum is an arithmetic problem
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: A workplace problem involves something huge.
explanation.definitionFit: This American marsupial is an example of an animal.

clue.text: A hybrid tea said to be a talisman

parts.note: a mule is a cross between a horse and a donkey

indicators.note: said means the drink's name is spoken, giving the sound of a letter

parts.note: the drink tea sounds like the letter T

explanation.surface: A hybrid tea rose is supposedly a lucky charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hybrid tea' is a well-known type of rose, which the parse splits apart.
explanation.definitionFit: An amulet is a charm worn to ward off evil, a kind of talisman.

clue.text: A good place to tie up the Confederate army?

definitions.text: A good place to tie up
definitions.meaning: the sheltered side of a ship or harbour, away from the wind, is a good place to moor
General Robert E. Lee led the Confederate army in the American Civil War, so it was his side

explanation.definitionFit: The side sheltered from the wind suits mooring, and General Lee's team in the Civil War was his side.

clue.text: Abandon Republican trapped by bear

indicators.note: the Republican's letter is enclosed within the word for bear

parts.note: to stand something is to bear or tolerate it

explanation.surface: A Republican caught by a bear is left in the lurch.
explanation.definitionFit: To strand someone is to leave them helpless, to abandon them.

clue.text: Bad idea not bringing in supervisors earlier

indicators.note: the shuffled letters take the supervisors inside them
a bad idea is a faulty one, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: foremen supervise workers

explanation.surface: It's a bad idea not to bring in supervisors sooner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' turns IDEA NOT into ATIONED, which goes around FOREMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Aforementioned describes something referred to earlier in a text, so it loosely means earlier.

clue.text: You might catch guy here running water in northeast

definitions.meaning: a guy rope or wire is fastened at a T-shaped fitting, and also 'guy' means tease, a word with the same sound
this river flows through northeast England, forming the old Yorkshire and County Durham boundary

explanation.definitionFit: T-shaped fixings are where guy lines are caught, and the river is flowing water in northeast England.

clue.text: Stand for artist, endlessly calm

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: an easel is a stand that holds a painter's canvas

explanation.surface: A painter's stand, going on forever, is soothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease is to calm or soothe pain or worry.

clue.text: Passenger going around with women's credentials everywhere

indicators.note: the passenger goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a fare is a paying passenger in a taxi
and means with, as in bread and butter
W is the abbreviation for women
ID is proof of identity

explanation.surface: A traveller carries women's identity papers on a wide journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Far and wide is an idiom for over a great area, in every place.

clue.text: Pack volunteers representative

parts.note: the TA, Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force
an MP, Member of Parliament, represents a constituency

explanation.surface: Volunteers pack around their elected representative.
explanation.definitionFit: To tamp is to pack something down firmly, as tobacco in a pipe.

clue.text: Desert more stormy loch

parts.note: wilder weather is more stormy
Loch Ness is the famous Scottish lake

explanation.surface: A desert grows more stormy than a Scottish loch.
explanation.definitionFit: A wilderness is an uninhabited, barren region, which a desert is.
